newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK lawyers bid for release of 4,000 boatpeople.
newsitem.headline: HK lawyers bid for release of 4,000 boatpeople.

text.p: Lawyers for Vietnamese asylum-seekers filed a suit in Hong Kong on Tuesday seeking the release of more than 4,000 boatpeople detained in camps in the British colony.
The legal defence group Refugee Concern lodged a habeas corpus case with the High Court.
The group argued that the Vietnamese, incarcerated for years, were being held illegally "for unreasonable periods".
"They are held in indefinite arbitrary detention while the Hong Kong government negotiates and hopes Vietnam will accept them back," Rob Brook of Refugee Concern told reporters.
"But there comes a point in time in terms of legality the detention becomes unreasonable, and these cases have become unreasonable," he said.
The Vietnamese government has so far not agreed to the repatriation of around 4,000 affected detainees who are held in closed camps in the colony.
The number of Vietnamese boatpeople in Hong Kong has been halved to a little under 10,000 this year through a combination of voluntary and forced returns to Vietnam.
Brook said the 4,000 had been in detention for up to eight years in some cases. Half the group were under 18, and most had "never run on grass, never touched a tree and never seen a dog".
The refugee lawyer said he was confident about the lawsuit, saying right was on the group's side.

The case brings additional pressure on the Hong Kong and British governments, already struggling with tension in the camps, pressure from China to evict the refugees and Vietnam's resistance to repatriation of thousands of unwanted boatpeople.
China has demanded that all Vietnamese camps in Hong Kong be emptied before Britain hands the territory over to Beijing at midnight next June 30.
The colonial administration has been on a drive to clear out all the detention camps before the handover.
Earlier on Tuesday, more than 240 boatpeople, including 67 women and 56 children, were flown back to Hanoi in the latest repatriation.
Several times this year tensions in the camps have exploded into fierce rioting and mass breakouts in a bid to fight deportation.
The detainees are the last of a flood of tens of thousands who fled Vietnam after the communists won the Vietnam War in 1975.
